categories.markdown:
## API requests and integration

API integration policy: keep API code separate from UI code; choose suitable query/state integration for the stack, prefer Axios as an HTTP client when appropriate, and avoid unnecessary requests, duplicated state, and unrelated renders. Axios is a preference, not a requirement to replace an already suitable transport. Library choice can be clarified with the user when the actual project context leaves a material choice unresolved; do not ask repeatedly when the stack or earlier decision already resolves it. For an unspecified stack, retain the established Redux Toolkit default and use RTK Query for server-data integration when applicable. The Redux Toolkit query system is named RTK Query, not Redux Query.

Axios sends HTTP requests. RTK Query or TanStack Query coordinates query identity, server data, request state, cache, and invalidation. These are complementary responsibilities, not competing names for the same layer. With Redux, RTK Query may use its existing base transport or an appropriate shared Axios-backed base query; with TanStack Query, query functions can call shared Axios service functions. Avoid installing or combining redundant clients and query systems merely to satisfy a checklist.

### Responsibility boundaries

| Layer | Owns | Does not duplicate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP client | Relevant service configuration, headers, timeouts, transport, and shared error/auth handling | UI-specific state, component rendering, or a second unmanaged response cache |
| Feature endpoints/services | Resource operations, request parameters, response transformation, and contract boundaries | Screen layout and unrelated feature logic |
| Query integration | Query identity, cached server data, request lifecycle, refresh/invalidation, and subscriptions | A competing copy of the same authoritative data in an ordinary UI slice |
| Hooks/adapters, where useful | Component-facing query use, selected results, and reusable feature behavior | A new generic wrapper that reimplements the chosen query library |
| UI | Rendering relevant data and states, collecting user intent, invoking actions | Scattered raw transport calls and ad hoc global caching logic |

Hooks are a suitable React integration point when the query library provides them or when a focused reusable feature hook helps. Plain service functions remain appropriate for framework-independent operations, jobs, and non-component consumers. Do not require every API function to be a hook, call hooks outside their supported context, or force extra wrappers around simple generated query hooks.

### Before implementing

Identify existing transport and query libraries, the endpoint contract, the operation's trigger and prerequisites, server-data ownership, query identity, freshness/retention needs, mutation effects, error/retry strategy, and expected UI states. Select API requests and integration, Caching and server data, State management and code organization, and Rendering performance, alongside relevant UI categories.

| ID | Guideline or requirement | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API-01 | Choose libraries according to the explicit stack and prior decisions. | Redux integrates with RTK Query when suitable; TanStack Query is used when selected. Axios remains the preferred suitable transport, not an automatic redundant dependency. |
| API-02 | Keep API configuration and endpoint definitions outside presentation components. | Relevant services share suitable configuration rather than repeating URLs, authentication, timeout, and error handling in every screen. |
| API-03 | Separate operations by feature or resource with meaningful responsibilities. | Endpoints and transformations are discoverable; one unstructured global service does not accumulate the whole application. |
| API-04 | Maintain an explicit request/response contract. | Methods, parameters, payloads, response shapes, pagination, and error cases are understood. Runtime validation is used where boundary risk warrants it; static types alone are not assumed to validate a server response. |
| API-05 | Use one authoritative server-data query owner for each resource flow. | The query result and pending/error state are not recopied into component state, Redux slices, and a second cache without a real purpose. Editable drafts are deliberate separate data. |
| API-06 | Use hooks or plain functions according to the execution context. | UI consumers use declarative query integration where appropriate; transport remains reusable. Avoid unnecessary custom wrappers and parallel effect-driven fetching. |
| API-07 | Trigger reads only when their prerequisites and task context are satisfied. | A missing record identifier, unresolved account, hidden inactive feature, or incomplete query does not cause an unintended request. Background prefetch is allowed when intentional. |
| API-08 | Do not start imperative requests directly during render. | Rendering does not itself launch a fresh raw request; supported query hooks describe the subscription and lifecycle. Mutations follow explicit user or business events. |
| API-09 | Include all response-changing inputs in query identity. | Filters, search, page, sort, record, and relevant account/tenant context yield correct separate results. Secrets are not needlessly embedded in query keys. |
| API-10 | Keep query infrastructure and relevant inputs stable within their intended lifecycle. | Recreating a query client, resetting its store, changing accidental keys, or wiring duplicate fetching does not repeatedly discard cache or resend requests. Server-rendered request isolation is respected where applicable. |
| API-11 | Propagate supported cancellation and protect against outdated responses. | Query cancellation signals reach the transport where supported; old search or record responses do not overwrite current intent. Cancellation is not assumed to undo a server-side write. |
| API-12 | Define realistic timeouts and bounded retry rules per operation. | Transient failures can recover without endless loops; ordinary validation or permission failures are not blindly retried. Writes are retried only when their semantics or an idempotency mechanism make it safe. No universal retry count or timeout is imposed. |
| API-13 | Coordinate authentication recovery without request storms. | Where refresh is supported, expired-session recovery is bounded, concurrent refreshes are coordinated, and unrecoverable authentication returns to the appropriate user flow. |
| API-14 | Define cache reuse, freshness, retention, and refetch per resource. | Default library behavior is understood; focus/reconnect refresh, polling, or subscription updates are intentional. Cached data is not assumed fresh merely because it remains in memory. |
| API-15 | Distinguish query caching from HTTP/browser/CDN caching and persistent storage. | Freshness-sensitive operations have appropriate behavior at the layers under the application's control; changing an in-memory cache option is not claimed to disable every network cache. |
| API-16 | Update or invalidate affected queries after writes. | Detail views, lists, counts, and filtered results converge to the correct outcome without unnecessarily refetching every resource. |
| API-17 | Handle optimistic writes and ambiguous failures deliberately. | Optimistic changes can roll back or reconcile; a timed-out write is not automatically assumed never to have reached the server. |
| API-18 | Present loading, refreshing, empty, error, success, and cancellation appropriately. | First load differs from refreshing existing data; useful old data may remain with clear refresh feedback. Canceled obsolete reads are not shown as alarming failures. Errors are not disguised as empty success. |
| API-19 | Subscribe and transform narrowly to avoid unrelated renders. | Consumers select relevant results, preserve useful identity, and avoid unnecessary repeated expensive transformations. Required data/state changes still render correctly. |
| API-20 | Treat request count as an observable outcome, not a zero-request promise. | Deduplication, pagination, input debouncing when useful, and cache reuse prevent unnecessary calls; intentional retries, refreshes, and changed inputs remain allowed. |
| API-21 | Respect resource and account lifecycles. | Cleanup, logout, and account changes cannot leave stale subscriptions or another user's records visible; credentials are not cached as ordinary response data or exposed in routine logging. |
| API-22 | Verify actual requests, cache, state, and rendering together. | Check initial load, multiple consumers, revisit, changed inputs, rapid switching, slow/failing requests, retry, mutation, and relevant auth changes. Inspect network behavior and render cost; an installed dependency or screenshot does not prove correctness. |

### Cache direction examples — contextual, not fixed rules

- Repeated reads of slowly changing reference data: reuse can help; define how changes become visible.
- Lists and record details: reusable cache can help navigation; keys and post-mutation invalidation must be correct.
- Fast-changing status: shorter acceptable staleness, deliberate refetch/polling, or live updates may be needed; no fixed lifetime is imposed.
- Consequential writes and authoritative validation: do not replace the server operation with a cached result or automatically replay unsafe writes.
- Sensitive or session-specific data: scope reuse deliberately; no blanket persistence and no cross-account reuse.
- One-off results with no meaningful reuse: avoid adding cache/invalidation complexity without benefit.

### After implementing

Record the chosen transport and query owner, feature boundaries, query inputs, cache/freshness policy, mutation invalidation, and verification evidence. Confirm both UI correctness and request behavior. Necessary refetches and re-renders are not failures; unexplained duplicates, stale responses, stale cache after mutations, and unrelated render work are defects to resolve.

References: [Axios: Creating an instance](https://axios-http.com/docs/instance), [Axios: Cancellation](https://axios-http.com/docs/cancellation), [RTK Query: Customizing queries](https://redux.js.org/toolkit/rtk-query/usage/customizing-queries), [RTK Query: Cache behavior](https://redux.js.org/toolkit/rtk-query/usage/cache-behavior), [TanStack Query: Cancellation](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-cancellation), [TanStack Query: Important defaults](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/important-defaults).

categories.title: Progressive web apps (PWA)
categories.appliesWhen: Installable web experience, service workers, offline behavior, persistent data, and updates
categories.markdown:
## Progressive web apps (PWA)

Treat a PWA as a usable web application with progressive capabilities, not just a manifest, icon, or install button. Explicit policy: offline mode and PWA-specific caching are disabled by default. Enable offline content, service-worker response caching, precaching, offline persistence, queued offline writes, or background synchronization only when the user explicitly requests or specifies them. Do not infer that requesting a PWA authorizes these features. Installation, push, and background capabilities differ by browser and platform; detect relevant support and preserve a usable browser experience.

This PWA policy governs app-added offline and persistent caching behavior. It does not by itself disable ordinary browser HTTP caching or an intentionally chosen in-memory API-query cache; those remain subject to the separate API and caching policies. It does not authorize adding persistence to a query cache. Do not claim all cache layers are disabled merely because PWA caching is disabled.

Checks that concern offline caches, persisted offline data, queued writes, synchronization, or a caching service worker are conditional on explicit user authorization. When these capabilities are off, mark those checks Not applicable and verify their absence. Network-failure feedback and ordinary browser usability still apply.

### Before building

Define supported environments, install experience, and update behavior. Record offline mode and PWA caching as Off unless explicitly requested; if requested, define offline task scope, cache boundaries, user/account data policy, and any pending-write synchronization. Reuse suitable project tooling rather than requiring one universal PWA library. Apply Responsive design, Accessibility, Color contrast, Typography and content, Navigation, State management, API requests, and Caching as applicable.

| ID | Guideline or requirement | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PWA-01 | Provide a secure production origin and a usable ordinary web experience. | Production uses HTTPS as applicable; users can perform supported browser tasks without installation or optional capabilities. Local-development exceptions do not justify insecure deployment. |
| PWA-02 | Define a correct web app manifest and suitable install assets. | Identity, name, launch URL, scope, display mode, and required platform icons are correct; icons, including suitable maskable assets where used, are not misleadingly cropped or missing. Check the intended browser's actual install requirements. |
| PWA-03 | Make installation optional, understandable, and platform-aware. | Install promotion appears only where meaningful and supported, handles dismissal, and is not repeatedly forced. Manual platform instructions or normal browser use remain possible when a custom prompt is unavailable. |
| PWA-04 | Verify installed navigation and launch behavior. | Launch and deep links open the intended screen; refresh and return work, navigation does not assume a browser toolbar exists, and external/out-of-scope links behave deliberately. |
| PWA-05 | Keep offline mode and PWA-specific caching off unless explicitly requested. When requested, define offline behavior per task rather than caching everything. | Without that request, no offline cache, precache, persisted offline data, or write queue is added. With that request, the supported offline scope is explicit and accurate. |
| PWA-06 | Separate offline, stale data, service failure, and authentication failure. | Appropriate messages and recovery paths are present; a connectivity hint alone is not assumed to prove the API is reachable. Cached data has appropriate freshness context. |
| PWA-07 | When a requested capability needs a service worker, give it a clear registration, scope, and lifecycle. | No cache-producing worker is added by default. A worker for another requested capability does not silently enable offline caching. Service workers are not described as universally required for browser installation. |
| PWA-08 | Only when PWA caching is explicitly requested, choose fetch/cache strategies according to resource purpose. | Static assets, navigation, and API reads have appropriate separate strategies. Do not blindly cache every request or error response. Mark this check Not applicable when PWA caching is off. |
| PWA-09 | Coordinate service-worker caches with query and HTTP caches. | RTK Query or TanStack Query freshness is not defeated by an independently stale service-worker response. Query invalidation alone is not claimed to purge every other cache layer. |
| PWA-10 | Preserve meaningful offline fallback routes. | Supported cached routes open where promised; unavailable routes show a useful fallback rather than a blank page or unrelated cached content. |
| PWA-11 | Handle updates without losing work or mixing incompatible versions. | A new worker/version activates at an appropriate time; forced reload or takeover does not silently erase drafts. The active page's assets and data/schema assumptions stay compatible. |
| PWA-12 | Clean up caches deliberately across versions and applications. | Retired caches are removed when safe; one app does not delete unrelated origin caches or assets still needed by active old-version sessions. |
| PWA-13 | Scope private data and offline storage to the intended session. | Logout/account changes cannot reveal another user's cached pages or records; credentials and sensitive responses are not persisted indiscriminately. Offline data access is a product decision, not a replacement for server authorization. |
| PWA-14 | Add offline durable storage only for explicitly requested offline features. | Appropriate draft or queue persistence is conditional, not automatic. An in-memory Redux/query cache is not assumed to survive app closure; UI state, offline storage, and worker execution remain separate. |
| PWA-15 | Handle storage limits, eviction, and migrations. | Writes and cache operations can fail gracefully; old persisted formats migrate safely or recover clearly. Browser storage is not promised to be a guaranteed backup. |
| PWA-16 | Queue offline writes only when the user explicitly requests the capability and the operation is suitable. | No queue is created by default. If enabled, pending/unsynced differs from server-confirmed; consequential or freshness-dependent operations may still require connectivity. |
| PWA-17 | Reconcile queued work after reconnection. | Ordering, duplicate prevention or idempotency, conflict handling, authentication expiry, and bounded retries are defined. A failed/uncertain write is not blindly replayed. |
| PWA-18 | Provide fallbacks for background synchronization and other optional capabilities. | Pending work can resume through supported foreground flows; the browser is not assumed to keep a worker alive or finish synchronization after the app closes. |
| PWA-19 | Ask for optional permissions in context. | Push and other permission requests follow a relevant user action and explanation; denial leaves the main app usable. Push is not required merely because the app is a PWA. |
| PWA-20 | Keep installed layouts usable with device and browser constraints. | Safe areas, standalone display, changing viewport height, mobile keyboard, zoom, and reduced motion preserve access and correct feedback. |
| PWA-21 | Coordinate multiple sessions where applicable. | Multiple tabs or installed windows do not produce duplicate queue submissions, conflicting updates, or stale account state. |
| PWA-22 | Verify actual lifecycle and offline behavior on supported environments. | Check browser and installed launch, install/dismiss, online/offline/slow network, cached and uncached routes, reconnection, session expiry, logout, pending writes, worker update with a draft open, and storage failure or loss. Mockups or manifest presence do not establish these behaviors. |

### After building

Record supported and unsupported capabilities, offline/PWA-cache settings, update policy, and verification evidence. Verify defaults remain off when not requested. Conditional offline/cache/sync checks are Not applicable with that reason; ordinary network-failure usability is still checked. If offline features were requested, record their precise scope and resource strategies and verify them. Test intended environments, installed mode, and any applicable worker lifecycle behavior.
